clue.text: 28 and 29 dabble and dawdle

definitions.meaning: Stephen ... the humorist and Dennis ... the dramatist share these names with two snooker champions
to dabble is to do something idly or without serious effort
to dawdle is to move about aimlessly and slowly

explanation.walkthrough: Besides the snooker player sense the theme uses, the cross-references point to Stephen Potter (author of Gamesmanship) and Dennis Potter (TV dramatist); the setter admitted it is a little circular.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers Stephen and Dennis share the surname, while the verb means to fiddle about idly or saunter.

clue.text: Basil, say, is not the same when in the lead

indicators.note: the clue says one piece is placed within the other, so these letters go inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
other means different, not the same

explanation.surface: Someone muses that basil behaves differently when it is out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is the metal, not leadership; its symbol PB is split open by OTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an example of a leafy herb used in cooking, which is what a potherb is.

clue.text: Punctuation expert offers support

definitions.meaning: Lynne ... wrote the bestselling punctuation guide Eats, Shoots and Leaves
a framework of beams holding up a roof, or a surgical belt for a hernia

explanation.walkthrough: Lynne Truss is a British writer whose book on punctuation was a surprise bestseller.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known author on punctuation shares her surname with a supporting frame or hernia belt.

clue.text: For a short while, divers help me breathe in time

indicators.note: to breathe something in is to take it inside, so the shuffled letters enclose the next piece
divers is an old word for various or assorted, so these letters are put into a varied order

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Scuba divers ask for help to breathe for a little while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is the adjective meaning sundry, not people underwater; it scrambles HELP ME into EPHEML, which takes in ERA after its fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ephemeral lasts only briefly, existing for a short time before passing.

clue.text: Fellow actor and director in Big Apple

parts.note: a co-star is an actor sharing top billing

explanation.surface: A co-star and the film's director are in New York City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big Apple' looks like New York but is literal: the costard is a large old English cooking apple. 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The costard is a large ribbed variety of English apple, so a big apple indeed.

clue.text: Man on board Queen's in good mood

indicators.note: the clue places the monarch's letters inside the word for high spirits

parts.note: cheer means good spirits or a happy mood
QU is an abbreviation for queen; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A man aboard ship notes that the Queen is in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor; it is a draughts piece on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequer is a counter in the board game draughts, the pieces being called men.

clue.text: Oasis a help crossing this

indicators.note: the region's name runs across the boundaries of the first three words of the clue

explanation.surface: Travellers over a desert region would find a watering hole useful.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: an oasis would help anyone crossing the Sahel, the semi-arid belt south of the Sahara.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahel is the dry belt of land on the southern fringe of the Sahara desert, where an oasis is welcome.

clue.text: He's ambitious to get exceptional site in Riviera resort

indicators.note: the selected letters go inside the rearranged coast name
to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters of the French coast's name are rearranged
the setter's twist on odd: taking every other letter, excepting the rest

explanation.surface: An ambitious man wants a remarkable plot on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town but means sort again; 'exceptional' is the setter's fresh twist on 'odd', keeping alternate letters. 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An arriviste is a pushy newcomer, a social climber ambitious for status.

clue.text: With no bird, 19 down's at home with golf on line, perhaps

indicators.note: with no signals that something is removed from the cross-referenced name

parts.note: the cross-reference is the snooker player's surname
a hen is a female bird
in means at home
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Without his chicken, a snooker player relaxes at home with a round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing HEN from HENDRY leaves DRY; the definition is washing pegged out on a clothes line.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry on a clothes line is hung up to lose its moisture, the definition giving an example.

clue.text: Trinkets cannot possibly produce a junction box

indicators.note: possibly signals a rearrangement in which the letters of one word, plus the answer, make up the phrase

explanation.surface: An electrician denies that trinkets could ever make a junction box.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the letters of A JUNCTION BOX equal CANNOT plus the answer, so remove CANNOT and rearrange the remaining J, U, I, B, O, X.
explanation.definitionFit: Bijoux is the French plural for jewels, used in English for small ornaments or trinkets.

clue.text: Hole cut in poor side at Twickenham

indicators.note: poor suggests something badly made, so these letters are put together differently

explanation.surface: A hole has been dug in a feeble rugby pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is England's national rugby stadium in London; the line along the side of the pitch is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The boundary marking along each side of a rugby pitch is called this.

clue.text: Rolls in hay for a 1 across

indicators.note: the luxury car abbreviation goes inside the dried grass

parts.note: taken as written
RR is the abbreviation for Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles in a haystack in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' is the car, not tumbling. Harry Potter is the boy wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional schoolboy wizard J.K. Rowling created carries the theme surname.

clue.text: Some worried about parking in race venue

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the parking symbol
worried here means shaken or troubled, so these letters are disturbed

parts.note: P is the road sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Racegoers fret about parking at the course.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom Downs in Surrey hosts the Derby horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Surrey racecourse is home to the Derby, one of Britain's great flat races.

clue.text: A 1 across (Crucible's favourite?) could be cast as villainous, not having one

indicators.note: casting is shaping anew, so the letters are remodelled after the removal

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A snooker player, the setter's favourite, could be cast as a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: VILLAINOUS minus I ('not having one') is rearranged. Ronnie O'Sullivan is a snooker champion, and the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield hosts the world championship, hence the setter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronnie O'Sullivan is a multiple world champion snooker player, a famous potter of balls.

clue.text: A 1 across thumped old farceur

parts.note: beat means struck or thumped
Brian Rix was a British actor famous for Whitehall farces

explanation.surface: A snooker player hit an elderly comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Rix led long-running stage farces in London's West End; Beatrix Potter wrote the Peter Rabbit books.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's author of Peter Rabbit was Beatrix Potter, sharing the theme surname.

clue.text: A sample receives rare approval in one go

indicators.note: receives means the sample word takes in the other letters

parts.note: a taste is a small sample
R is listed in Collins as an abbreviation for rare
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: A small sample is unusually well received, all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: R for 'rare' is uncommon but in Collins.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means with one single action, all at once, just as doing something in one go.

clue.text: Salad ingredient is hard to chew

indicators.note: chewing mashes things up, so these letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something in the salad is tough to chew.
explanation.definitionFit: The crisp red root vegetable is often sliced into salads.

clue.text: 1 across's product's feet not accepted in US state

indicators.note: the abbreviation for feet goes inside the trimmed state name
not signals that the letter for accepted is left out of the state

parts.note: Delaware is a US state

explanation.surface: A potter's wares are refused entry to an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not accepted' looks like a single idea but splits: 'not' is the deletion signal and 'accepted' its abbreviation A. Delft in the Netherlands gave its name to blue-and-white glazed pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Glazed earthenware made in the Dutch town of Delft is what such a craftsman produces.

clue.text: See 29
Scratch rear end enough to need surgery

indicators.note: the end of the word rear is its final letter
something needing surgery is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's backside is so sore it needs an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear end' looks like a backside but just means the last letter of 'rear'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scratch a surface is to make it coarse or uneven, to rough it up.

clue.text: Gather about a pound for old weapon

indicators.note: the gathering word goes about the other letters

parts.note: to herd is to gather animals together
LB is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: Collect about a pound for an antique weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A halberd is a combined spear and battleaxe used in medieval warfare.

clue.text: See 28
They're hot and dry courses, not small

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for small is dropped from the courses

parts.note: desserts are courses of a meal

explanation.surface: Puddings are hot and dry courses, though not small portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' is meal courses, the puddings, not racecourses; drop one S.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid regions like the Sahara are the classic example of hot, dry land.

clue.text: Meats go off when brought in on sabbath

indicators.note: the word for when is brought inside the word for decay

parts.note: to rot is to go off or decay
as can mean when

explanation.surface: Meat spoils if it is brought in on the day of rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasts are joints of meat cooked in the oven.

clue.text: Result has old fellow in the wrong order

indicators.note: has means the result word contains the other letters

parts.note: outturn means output or result

explanation.surface: The outcome is an old chap placed in the wrong sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' belongs to the definition, not the container: OUTTURN has O and F within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking or acting out of turn is doing so at the wrong moment or position in the sequence.

clue.text: Chilly novel

definitions.meaning: cool and breezy, as a brisk wind

explanation.definitionFit: A brisk cold wind is fresh, and so is a new or original idea.

clue.text: Pots remodelled to hide unknown errors

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hide the unknown inside them
remodelled means the pots are reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A potter's pots, remodelled, conceal errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Typos are typing mistakes, small printing errors.

clue.text: Opportunity for 12 to give plant a better chance of success

definitions.meaning: in snooker, a ball that can be sunk is a chance for the 12 across player

definitions.text: give plant a better chance of success
definitions.meaning: to move a plant into a bigger pot

explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is the snooker player Ronnie O'Sullivan.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball lined up to sink is a snooker term; gardeners also transfer seedlings to larger containers.

clue.text: A 1 across's special poem

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the definition means a potter is

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A potter's special verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Josiah Spode founded the famous Stoke-on-Trent pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Josiah Spode was an English ceramics maker of Stoke-on-Trent, whose firm kept the family name.

clue.text: Father demolished housing before, following this

indicators.note: housing means the rebuilt letters contain the next piece
demolished means knocked down, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A father's house is knocked down and something comes after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' gives HAFTER, which 'housing' wraps round its insert after the first letter; 'following this' is an adverbial definition, as in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereafter is an adverb meaning from now on, after this point.

clue.text: Females on stage forget their words for a 1 across

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the preceding word

parts.note: a step is a stage in a process
hens are female birds; the plural gives two of them
actors who dry forget their lines

explanation.surface: Actresses on stage forget their lines in front of a snooker player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Females' gives HEN twice, two hens. Stephen Hendry won the snooker world title a record seven times.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish seven-time world snooker champion is a famous potter of balls.

clue.text: Almost all royalty grievously erred in backing a 1 across

indicators.note: backing means everything is read in reverse
grievously suggests something badly hurt, so the letters are mangled
almost all means the final letter of royalty is dropped

parts.note: sinned means erred

explanation.surface: Most of the royal family behaved badly in supporting a snooker player.
explanation.walkthrough: ROYALT is scrambled to ROLYAT, then ROLYAT plus SINNED read backwards gives the whole name. Dennis Taylor won the 1985 world snooker final on the last black.
explanation.definitionFit: The Northern Irish 1985 world snooker champion is a famous potter of balls.
